latin.485: Respondeo distinguendum esse nomen παράπτωμα à duobus aliis: Illo enim Apostolus modo peccatum Adami, modo vitium ex peccato Adami in omnibus hominibus ortum designat: His solum peccatum Adami significat, non quidem actuale praecisum ab habituali, sed simul cum habituali. Itaque quantum ad hoc nomen παράπτωμα attinet, nego Maiorem: quantum vero ad alia duo, nego minorem.
latin.486: Deinde nego Apostolum ullo eorum trium nominum peccatum actuale Adami designasse praecisum à corruptione quam in Adamo peperit, cum tamen de peccato actuali ita praeciso intelligenda sit haec nostra controversia. Vis enim peccato illo suo actuali Adamum meruisse cum sibi tum nobis illam corruptionem. Non ergo potes probare per ἁμαρτίαν hoc loco peccatum actuale Adami esse intelligendum.
latin.487: Fac tamen intelligi; negabo peccatum illud introiisse in mundum per imputationem: sed dici introiisse in mundum, quia suum venenum reliquit in Adamo, quod sine eiusmodi imputatione serpsit ab Adamo in Sethum, à Setho in Enosch, ab hoc in Kenanem, & ita paulatim à patre in filios manavit, donec ad nos perveniret propagatione & multiplicatione naturali.
latin.488: Sustinui impetum tuum, vide an possis meum. Hinc enim mihi surgit argumentum tuam evertens sententiam. Dabis mihi profecto dogma illud de imputatione peccati actualis Adami toti generi humano, si verum est, si credendum est, doceri alicubi in Scriptura absolutissima fidei nostrae norma. Dabis etiam, sicubi docetur, doceri in hoc loco, ubi Apostolus quicquid ab Adamo mali in humanum genus manavit explicat accurate. Dabis tandem quaecunque mala Adamus cum posteris suis communicavit, ea ab Apostolo revocari ad haec duo, peccatum & mortem.
latin.489: Videamus ergo quodnam peccatum intelligat. Tu vis esse peccatum actuale Adami imputatum omnibus hominibus ad duas poenas, privationem justitiae originalis seu vitium originale, & mortem. Ego dico esse vitium originale seu corruptionem haereditariam in singulis hominibus inhaerentem, non autem peccatum actuale Adami singulis hominibus immediate imputatum. Tuam sententiam, quas attulisti, rationes non probant: iis enim, ut vides, respondi.
latin.490: Ego meam sic probo. Si quod peccatum Apostolus docet Rom. v. fuisse ab Adamo cum omnibus hominibus communicatum, illud profecto est, quod per Adamum docet in mundum introiisse, & per id mortem, ita ut mors in omnes homines pertransierit. Atqui peccatum illud, quod docet per Adamum in mundum introiisse, & per id mortem, est corruptio haereditaria, non autem peccatum actuale Adami praecise sumptum. Ergo si aliquod peccatum Apostolus docet, uti revera docet, ab Adamo cum omnibus hominibus communicatum, illud profecto est corruptio haereditaria, non autem peccatum actuale Adami. Maiorem non negabis: est enim manifesta. Certe peccatum per quod ait mortem introiisse in mundum, hoc est, ut ipse exponit, & tu post eum, in omnes homines, est illud cui proxime generis humani mortem & condemnationem ascribit. Minorem probo. Primam rationem mihi ministrat ipsum nomen peccati ἡ ἁμαρτία: sic enim (ut doctissimus Beza ad hunc versum notavit) vocare solet Apostolus morbum illum haereditarium: adeo quidem ut vix apud Paulum addito articulo aliud declaret. Morbus autem haereditarius non est peccatum actuale Adami, sed corruptio, & vitium ab illo ortum.

pass_a.485: I answer: split παράπτωμα from the other two. With that one name Paul sometimes marks Adam's sin, sometimes the vice born from it in all humans; with the other two he marks only Adam's sin—not actual sliced off from habitual, but actual-together-with-habitual. So for παράπτωμα I deny the major; for the other two, the minor.
pass_a.486: Next I deny that by any of the three names Paul marked Adam's actual cut clean from the corruption it bred in him—yet our fight is about actual so cut. You want that lone actual to have earned the corruption for him and for us. You cannot prove, then, that ἁμαρτία here must mean that bare actual.
pass_a.487: Grant the sense for a moment; I still deny entry into the world by imputation. 'Entered' means he left his venom in Adam, and without that kind of reckoning it crept Adam→Seth→Enosh→Kenan and so by degrees father to sons until it reached us by natural begetting and increase.
pass_a.488: I have borne your charge; see if you can bear mine. From here rises a stroke that overturns your view. You will grant me that the dogma of imputing Adam's actual to the whole human race, if true and to be believed, is taught somewhere in Scripture, our most absolute rule of faith. You will grant too that if taught anywhere, it is taught here, where Paul carefully lays out whatever evil flowed from Adam into the race. And you will grant at last that whatever evils Adam shared with his posterity Paul reduces to these two: sin and death.
pass_a.489: So which sin does he mean? You will have Adam's actual imputed to all for two penalties—loss of original righteousness / original vice, and death. I say it is original vice or hereditary corruption inhering in each person, not Adam's actual immediately imputed to each. The reasons you brought do not prove your view: as you see, I have answered them.
pass_a.490: I prove mine thus. If Romans 5 teaches some sin shared from Adam with all, it is surely the one he says entered the world through Adam and death through it, so death passed upon all. But that entered-sin is hereditary corruption, not Adam's actual taken precisely. Therefore the shared sin he teaches is hereditary corruption, not that bare actual. You will not deny the major—it is plain. The sin through which death entered the world (into all, as he and you after him expose) is what he nearest ascribes the race's death and condemnation to. I prove the minor. First help: the very name ἡ ἁμαρτία—so (Beza on this verse) Paul usually names that hereditary disease, and with the article scarcely marks anything else. A hereditary disease is not Adam's actual but corruption and vice sprung from it. Tip before GAR.

485: I answer that the name paraptoma must be distinguished from the other two: For by that one the Apostle sometimes designates Adam's sin, sometimes the vice arisen from Adam's sin in all humans: By these he signifies only Adam's sin, not indeed the actual cut off from the habitual, but together with the habitual. And so as far as this name paraptoma is concerned, I deny the Major: but as far as the other two, I deny the minor.
486: Next I deny that the Apostle by any of those three names designated Adam's actual sin cut off from the corruption which it produced in Adam, although yet this our controversy must be understood of actual sin so cut off. For you will have it that by that actual sin of his Adam earned that corruption both for himself and for us. You cannot therefore prove that by hamartia in this place Adam's actual sin must be understood.
487: Grant nevertheless that it is so understood; I will deny that that sin entered into the world by imputation. Rather it is said to have entered into the world, because he left his venom in Adam, which without that kind of imputation crept from Adam into Seth, from Seth into Enosh, from him into Kenan, and so little by little flowed from father into sons, until it reached us by natural propagation and multiplication.
488: I have sustained your assault; see whether you can sustain mine. For from here rises for me an argument overturning your opinion. You will certainly grant me that dogma concerning the imputation of Adam's actual sin to the whole human race, if it is true, if it must be believed, is taught somewhere in Scripture, the most absolute norm of our faith. You will also grant that, if it is taught anywhere, it is taught in this place, where the Apostle accurately explains whatever evil flowed from Adam into the human race. You will grant at last that whatever evils Adam communicated with his posterity, those the Apostle reduces to these two, sin and death.
489: Let us see therefore which sin he understands. You will have it to be Adam's actual sin imputed to all humans unto two penalties, the privation of original righteousness or original vice, and death. I say it is original vice or hereditary corruption inhering in individual humans, but not Adam's actual sin immediately imputed to individual humans. Your opinion the reasons you brought do not prove: for to them, as you see, I have replied.
490: I prove mine thus. If any sin the Apostle teaches in Rom. 5. was communicated by Adam with all humans, that certainly is what he teaches entered into the world through Adam, and through it death, so that death passed through unto all humans. But that sin which he teaches entered into the world through Adam, and through it death, is hereditary corruption, not however Adam's actual sin taken precisely. Therefore if the Apostle teaches any sin, as he truly does, communicated by Adam with all humans, that certainly is hereditary corruption, not however Adam's actual sin. You will not deny the Major: for it is manifest. Certainly the sin through which he says death entered into the world, that is, as he himself exposes, and you after him, into all humans, is that to which he nearest ascribes the death and condemnation of the human race. I prove the Minor. The first reason the very name of sin he hamartia supplies me: for so (as the most learned Beza noted on this verse) the Apostle is accustomed to call that hereditary disease: so much so that scarcely in Paul with the article added does it declare anything else. But a hereditary disease is not Adam's actual sin, but corruption, and vice arisen from it.
